summary_hint: <document_or_order_type> in <case_caption> (<court_name>, case <case_number>), entered <entry_or_order_date>: <support_awards summary> — the obligation type, amount, and END date IN-13 needs for continuance

typed_core.name: court_name
typed_core.why: identity/source — which court issued the order; third-party independence

typed_core.name: case_number
typed_core.why: identity/dedup — the case identifier for cross-document matching (confidential)

typed_core.name: case_caption
typed_core.why: identity — 'Petitioner v. Respondent'; names the parties for borrower attribution

typed_core.name: document_or_order_type
typed_core.why: IN-13 (rule reads it) — 'detect the income type': divorce decree / child-support order / alimony / support modification

typed_core.name: entry_or_order_date
typed_core.why: IN-13 — when the order took effect; recency; the anchor for computing remaining continuance

typed_core.name: effective_date
typed_core.why: disambiguator — support may start on a date other than entry (retroactive/prospective start)

typed_core.name: final_or_interlocutory_status
typed_core.why: processor/IN-13 — only a FINAL order is reliable for qualifying income; an interlocutory/temporary order is not
typed_core.prompt_hint: Only a final order is reliable; flag temporary/interlocutory orders

typed_core.name: obligee_name
typed_core.why: identity — who RECEIVES the support = the borrower using it to qualify (IN-13 attribution)

typed_core.name: current_compliance_or_enforcement_status
typed_core.why: IN-13 — corroborates receipt / history of payment vs arrears/enforcement

typed_core.name: judge_name_and_signature
typed_core.why: authenticity/execution — a court order is only valid if entered by the judge

nested_lists.name: support_awards
nested_lists.shape_reason: a decree commonly grants 1-4 obligations (alimony, child support, arrears, property offset) — few items, so a flat row is light and adequate; per-field wrapping is unnecessary

fields.name: award_type
fields.why: IN-13 — the obligation type per stream (alimony / child-support / spousal)

fields.name: amount
fields.why: IN-13 — the support amount per stream

fields.name: frequency
fields.why: IN-13 — monthly/weekly/lump; the amount is meaningless without its frequency [RULE FLOOR — absent from catalog as a named field]

fields.name: end_date
fields.why: IN-13 — the continuance/termination date the rule turns on ('order ends in 12 months -> may not be usable'); has no named catalog field [RULE FLOOR — absent from catalog]

fields.name: payer
fields.why: IN-13 — the obligor for this stream

fields.name: payee
fields.why: IN-13 — the obligee for this stream (borrower attribution)

fields.name: escalation_or_conditions
fields.why: IN-13 — verbatim escalation/condition, incl. event-based termination ('until the child turns 18') when end_date is not a stated date

fields.name: source
fields.why: provenance — where in the order this award was read

rejected.name: document_title, form_number, form_revision_date
rejected.reason: classification/version before extraction

rejected.name: issuer_name
rejected.reason: duplicates court_name

rejected.name: issuer_address, issuer_phone, issuer_email_or_url
rejected.reason: court contact; catch-all

rejected.name: document_issue_date
rejected.reason: duplicates entry_or_order_date

rejected.name: expiration_date
rejected.reason: support end dates live in support_awards.end_date, not a document expiry

rejected.name: statement_period_start/_end
rejected.reason: not applicable

rejected.name: party_names, party_addresses, parties
rejected.reason: covered by case_caption + flattened obligor/obligee + the award payer/payee columns

rejected.name: property_address, loan_number
rejected.reason: present only if the order awards specific property; catch-all unless a rule needs it

rejected.name: account_case_reference_number
rejected.reason: duplicates case_number

rejected.name: filing_date, hearing_date
rejected.reason: procedural; not what IN-13 reads; catch-all

rejected.name: signature_blocks
rejected.reason: judge signature is captured; party signatures marginal

rejected.name: notary_block, clerk_stamp_or_certification
rejected.reason: authenticity marginal beyond judge signature; catch-all

rejected.name: document_status_or_version
rejected.reason: final_or_interlocutory_status carries the material distinction

rejected.name: court_findings
rejected.reason: narrative; a conclusion of the court, not a fact IN-13 computes; catch-all

rejected.name: property_or_title_awards, debt_allocations
rejected.reason: not income-continuance; no IN-13 consumer; catch-all

rejected.name: restraining_lien_or_garnishment_terms
rejected.reason: not income; catch-all

rejected.name: compliance_deadlines
rejected.reason: procedural deadlines; not the support end date; catch-all

rejected.name: appeal_stay_or_modification_status
rejected.reason: marginal; catch-all

rejected.name: incorporated_agreements_or_exhibits
rejected.reason: noted in prompt; a reference list with no IN-13 field to feed; catch-all

rejected.name: subsequent_orders_or_amendments
rejected.reason: if a later order modifies terms it is its own document; catch-all

encoding_variations: document_or_order_type — no enum coercer; 'Final Judgment of Dissolution of Marriage', 'Order for Child Support', 'Marital Settlement Agreement (incorporated)', 'Uniform Support Order', 'Judgment/Decree'. Degrade to str

support amount + frequency — stated as '$1,500/month', '$750 semi-monthly', '$18,000 per year', or a per-child amount; the amount is meaningless without its frequency (a disambiguator carried as its own column)

end_date / termination — encoded as an explicit date, 'until the child reaches 18/graduates', 'for 36 months', or 'until remarriage/death'. Some are event-conditioned, not a date — capture verbatim and flag when non-numeric

open_questions.q: Flatten primary support vs nest support_awards — an order can grant alimony AND child support with different amounts/end dates
options: flatten only the primary award to typed fields (loses the second stream)
open_questions.recommendation: (b) — IN-13 must see every continuing stream and its end date GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): BUILD IT — LP-437 made nested lists cheap (one declaration + the generic mechanism); the one-list-budget / defer / no-consumer concern is overturned. Build as flat_row; the per-rule consumer is separate follow-up.

open_questions.q: Event-based termination — many child-support orders end on an event ('until the child turns 18'), not a date. end_date cannot always be a date
options: coerce end_date to date when stated + carry verbatim condition in escalation_or_conditions
open_questions.recommendation: keep end_date as the coerced date when a date is stated, and carry the verbatim condition in escalation_or_conditions; flag event-based terminations for human review rather than deriving a date

open_questions.q: Underivable specifics — IN-13's how_engine_checks derives type + amount + end date + receipt cleanly; it does not derive custody or property terms
open_questions.recommendation: confirm the support_awards columns are the right floor; custody/property terms correctly left to the catch-all

open_questions.q: Rule-floor gap registration — support_awards.end_date and .frequency are absent from the catalog
options: add them as first-class extracted values via the nested list
open_questions.recommendation: confirm they are added as first-class extracted values (via the nested list) so IN-13 is not dead on arrival GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): BUILD IT — LP-437 made nested lists cheap (one declaration + the generic mechanism); the one-list-budget / defer / no-consumer concern is overturned. Build as flat_row; the per-rule consumer is separate follow-up.

notes: No existing_extractor for this document type — new schema.

12 typed-core rows + one nested list. The decisive continuance data — type, amount, frequency, start, and END date per obligation — lives in support_awards because an order can grant more than one stream (alimony and child support). Below the 20-25 target, expected for a one-rule document.

RULE FLOOR find: support_awards.end_date is the field IN-13's example turns on and has no named catalog field (buried inside support_or_income_awards/ordered_obligations object[] blobs); frequency is likewise absent as a named field. Surfacing them as explicit columns is the primary rule-floor find. nested-list fields carry no rule_floor key in this format, so it is recorded here.

PII: no new _PII_FIELDS registration proposed. Party names (obligor/obligee) are standard sensitivity; case_number is confidential but a docket identifier, not a maskable PII kind. Family-law orders frequently contain children's names/DOBs and parties' SSNs in the body — these must NOT be captured to the unmasked catch-all; the prompt should be told to omit minors' identifying details.
An order may incorporate a Marital Settlement Agreement by reference — note it; the actual terms may be in the attached MSA.

judge_name_and_signature carries reason_class 'authenticity/execution' in the doc, which is not one of the five classes; mapped to processor (validity/authenticity gate) as a best guess — flagged as ambiguity.
